name: American Tower

header.one_liner: Global tower landlord with a fast-growing data center arm; slow tower growth, 17x AFFO and a 3.8% yield.
header.thesis: American Tower raised its 2026 outlook for the third time: AFFO per share is guided up about 3% to $11.10 at the midpoint, with CoreSite data centers growing 16% while US and Canada tower revenue falls about 3% on lower straight-line revenue. Leverage is down to 4.9x and buybacks are back. The stock is priced for the slow growth it delivers.

base.eps_label: FY2026E AFFO per share (the REIT measure of recurring cash earnings): midpoint of guidance $11.04 to $11.16. Multiples on this page are price to AFFO.
base.rev_label: FY2026E total revenue ($B): property revenue guidance midpoint $10.825B plus services

rev_cagr.why: Property revenue is guided up 5% in 2026 at the midpoint, with Data Centers +16%, Africa & APAC +16%, Latin America +11% and Europe +10%, but US & Canada -3% including a negative straight-line effect of over 3%. Organic tenant billings grew only 1.1% in the quarter. The base case assumes about 4% a year.
rev_cagr.source: American Tower Q3 2026 release (2026 outlook by segment)

margin_end.why: AFFO is about 47% of revenue. Data centers and buybacks help; higher interest costs on refinanced debt and international currency moves hurt. The base case holds it roughly flat.

share_chg.why: American Tower bought back $315M of stock in the quarter and the board added $2.0B of authorisation on top of $1.1B remaining. The base case assumes about 1% a year.

exit_pe.why: The stock trades at about 17x 2026 AFFO. The base case holds that multiple: low growth offsets the lower leverage. The bear case is a further de-rating if US carrier spending stays weak.
exit_pe.source: Engine judgment; current multiple computed from price and AFFO guidance

pillars.title: Data centers are the growth
pillars.claim: Data Centers cash revenue grew 16.3% and the segment is guided up about 16% for 2026.

evidence.t: Data Centers property revenue guidance $1,218M to $1,228M

pillars.test: Does CoreSite keep growing double digits as AI demand shifts to larger campuses?

pillars.title: US towers are slow
pillars.claim: Organic tenant billings grew 1.1%; US & Canada property revenue is guided down about 3%, mostly from lower straight-line revenue.
pillars.test: Does US carrier leasing pick up in 2027?

pillars.title: Balance sheet repaired
pillars.claim: Net leverage is 4.9x annualised adjusted EBITDA, low enough to restart buybacks.
pillars.test: Does leverage stay near 5x while buybacks continue?

pillars.title: Portfolio simplified
pillars.claim: The company is selling its Canadian towers for about $202M after earlier exits; the portfolio is more focused.

evidence.t: Sale of Canadian subsidiaries for about C$288M, closing Q4 2026

pillars.test: Is capital recycled into higher-growth assets or buybacks?

variant.street: The market pays about 17x AFFO and a 3.8% dividend yield for slow but secure tower cash flows.
variant.ours: A fair price for a slow-growing, contracted business. Our base case grows AFFO per share about 5% a year with the multiple held, which earns about the cost of equity.
variant.could_be_wrong: If US carriers step up 5G and AI-related network spending, organic growth could return to 4% to 5% and the multiple would rise.
variant.would_change_mind: Organic tenant billings growth back above 4%, or the price nearer 14x AFFO.

review.basis: Q3 2026 10-Q and release (quarter to 30 September 2026). Q4 and the 2027 outlook come in February; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: Towers grow slowly, data centers fast. At 17x AFFO with leverage repaired, the stock is fairly priced.
review.model: American Tower owns more than 100,000 communications sites worldwide and leases space on them to mobile carriers under long contracts with annual escalators. It also owns CoreSite data centers in the US.

how_it_earns.v: Leases to AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile with fixed escalators. The largest profit pool.
Latin America, Africa, Asia-Pacific and Europe; faster growth, currency risk.
CoreSite: interconnection-heavy data centers. Growing about 16%.
Site development and zoning for carriers. Small and volatile.

mix.note: Reported property segments. Operating margin is segment gross margin over segment revenue.

review.position: The largest independent tower company in the world, ahead of Crown Castle and SBA Communications.

sources: Tower sites that are hard to replicate
moat.threat: Carrier consolidation and lower network spending; satellite connectivity at the edges.

what_numbers_say.d: $2.87 in Q3; full year guided $11.04 to $11.16.
Organic tenant billings; total property revenue +4.5%.
CoreSite cash revenue growth, outlook raised again.
Net debt $35.7B; buybacks resumed with $3.1B available.

balance.read: Leverage down to 4.9x, investment grade, refinancing maturities steadily.
facts: $1.6B of new notes issued in September; $1.6B repaid in September and October

flags.evidence: Non-cash straight-line revenue swung to -$24M from +$28M, lowering reported growth about 2 points this year.
Unrealised losses of about $72M on equity investments lowered net income in the quarter.
Organic tenant billings growth of 1.1% is low for a tower company.

forecast_basis.rev_cagr: Sourced: segment outlook, slow US towers and fast data centers
forecast_basis.share_chg: Sourced: buybacks under the enlarged program

base.story: Towers grow low single digits, data centers mid-teens; AFFO per share grows about 5% with buybacks.

downside.story: Carrier spending stays weak and rates stay high; the multiple falls toward 14x AFFO.

upside.story: Carrier leasing recovers with new network builds and AI traffic; organic growth returns to 4% to 5%.

risks.how: US carriers have cut network capex; tower leasing slows with it.
A leveraged REIT refinances debt at higher rates and competes with bond yields.
International towers earn in local currencies; a strong dollar lowers reported results.
Hyperscalers build their own capacity; CoreSite depends on interconnection demand.
Mergers and exits remove tenants from shared sites.

peer_read.why_premium: American Tower has the most diversified portfolio, the data center business and the lowest leverage among the three US tower companies.
peer_read.why_not: SBA Communications trades at a lower GAAP multiple, and Crown Castle offers more US-only exposure for a recovery.
peer_read.peers_note: Peer P/E multiples are on GAAP earnings; tower companies are usually compared on price to AFFO, which this page uses for the target.

questions: When does US carrier leasing recover?
Is CoreSite worth more inside American Tower or outside it?
What return does a 3.8% yield plus 5% growth give against a 9% cost of equity?

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Property revenue grew 4.5% in the third quarter, but organic tenant billings only 1.1%. Data centers grew 16% and the full-year outlook was raised for the third time.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: Tower sites that are hard to replicate, long contracts with escalators and several tenants per tower. Carrier consolidation and lower network spending are the threats.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: Property gross margin is 73.5% and adjusted EBITDA margin 65.8%. AFFO per share grew 3.2% to $2.87.

arguments.label: Capital
arguments.text: Net leverage fell to 4.9x, buybacks resumed and the board added $2.0B of authorisation. The dividend yields about 3.8%.

thesis_long: American Tower is a landlord to mobile carriers and data center tenants. Its tower leases run for years with built-in escalators, and its CoreSite data centers are growing about 16% a year. This year the company raised its outlook three times, cut leverage to 4.9x and restarted buybacks.

The weak spot is US towers. Organic tenant billings grew only 1.1% in the quarter and US & Canada property revenue is guided down about 3%, partly because non-cash straight-line revenue is shrinking but also because carriers are spending less on networks. Growth now depends on international escalators and data centers.

Our base case grows AFFO per share about 5% a year with the multiple held near 17x, which with a 3.8% dividend earns about the cost of equity over 12 months. We would turn positive if organic billings growth returned above 4%, and negative if it turned negative.

upside_risks.how: A new round of carrier network builds would lift organic growth quickly on a high-margin base.
A sale or separate valuation of the data center business could show more value than the blended multiple implies.
